record.paper_title: Variational principles in grid generation and geometric modelling: theoretical justifications and open problems
record.context_brief: Polyhedral-metric formulation of variational mapping problems
record.original_question: Can the quasi-isometric variational functional be formulated directly on manifolds equipped with polyhedral metrics, with extrema sought among bounded-curvature mappings, and can proportional convergence of such polyhedral metrics to a metric satisfying a tangent-cone condition be used to prove convergence of both functional values and weak gradients or Euler-Lagrange formulations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ and $N$ be two-dimensional manifolds, each equipped with a polyhedral metric (i.e., a metric arising from a triangulation by Euclidean triangles glued isometrically along edges, with cone-type singularities at vertices). For a Lipschitz mapping $f:M\to N$, define the quasi-isometric variational functional
$$ I(f) \;=\; \int_M \Big( \tfrac{1}{2}\,\big(\lambda_1(f)^2+\lambda_2(f)^2\big) \;+\; \Phi\!\big(\lambda_1(f)\lambda_2(f)\big) \Big)\,d\mu_M, $$
where $\lambda_1(f),\lambda_2(f)$ are the singular values of the differential $df$ (defined almost everywhere with respect to the polyhedral area measure $\mu_M$) and $\Phi:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ is a convex barrier with $\Phi(t)\to+\infty$ as $t\to 0^+$ that penalises non-injectivity. Restrict admissible mappings to the class of bounded-curvature mappings, namely those whose pull-back metric $f^*g_N$ is a metric of bounded integral curvature in the sense of Alexandrov.

Address the following:

(1) Show that $I(\cdot)$ is well-defined on this class, that minimisers (or critical points) exist among bounded-curvature mappings with prescribed boundary correspondence, and formulate the corresponding Euler–Lagrange system in a weak sense intrinsic to the polyhedral setting.

(2) Suppose $(M_n,g_n)$ and $(N_n,h_n)$ are sequences of polyhedral metrics that converge proportionally (i.e., with uniformly bounded bi-Lipschitz distortion and vanishing distortion as $n\to\infty$) to metrics $(M,g)$ and $(N,h)$ that satisfy a tangent-cone condition: at every point the metric admits a unique metric tangent cone which is a Euclidean cone. Prove that if $f_n:M_n\to N_n$ are bounded-curvature minimisers (or weak Euler–Lagrange solutions) of the associated functionals $I_n$, then
$$ I_n(f_n)\longrightarrow I(f_\infty), \qquad df_n \rightharpoonup df_\infty \;\text{weakly}, $$
where $f_\infty$ is a bounded-curvature minimiser (or weak Euler–Lagrange solution) of $I$ on $(M,g)\to(N,h)$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned related work on discrete conformal geometry of polyhedral surfaces, quasi-isometric surface parameterisation, and convergence of bounded-curvature metrics, but no source establishes the full program of formulating the quasi-isometric variational functional on polyhedral manifolds with bounded-curvature mappings and proving proportional-convergence of values and weak gradients/Euler–Lagrange equations under a tangent-cone condition. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-isometric surface parameterization
status_evidence.snippet: Variational method for constructing quasi-isometric mappings; based on hyperelasticity existence theory, in smooth (not polyhedral) setting.
status_evidence.claim: Existing quasi-isometric variational theory is developed in smooth/continuous metric settings, not directly on polyhedral metrics.

status_evidence.title: Discrete conformal geometry of polyhedral surfaces and its convergence
status_evidence.snippet: Convergence results for polyhedral metrics approximating prescribed Riemann surface metrics.
status_evidence.claim: Convergence of polyhedral metrics to limit metrics is studied for conformal problems, but not for the quasi-isometric functional with bounded-curvature mapping class.
